system:
You extract quantitative facts about one clinical trial programme from one document.

Rules:
- Extract only facts stated in THIS document. Never use outside knowledge.
- Every fact needs "quote": an exact, verbatim span copied from the document (8-300 characters) that contains the number. Quotes are machine-checked; paraphrases are discarded.
- Placebo-adjusted values are preferred. If a value is within-arm (not placebo-adjusted), set attrs.placebo_adjusted=false.
- Units: keep the unit the document uses; put it in "unit".
- Other trials of the same investigational drug (phase 2, dose-finding, other populations, combination arms) belong
  to the programme: extract their facts too, and put the trial's name in attrs.trial when the document gives it.
- Return {"facts": []} only if the document reports no results for the investigational drug.

Allowed keys:
  n_randomized, median_followup, primary_endpoint, inclusion_threshold, planned_events, assumed_rrr, power,
  alpha, stopped_early, events_treatment, events_control, events_total, hr, ci_low, ci_high, p_value,
  biomarker_change, baseline_level, sbp_change, safety_signal, readout_statement

For biomarker_change and baseline_level, attrs must include: biomarker (one of LDL-C, non-HDL-C, apoB, HDL-C,
Lp(a), triglycerides, hsCRP, IL-6, Lp-PLA2 activity, sPLA2-IIA, SBP, other), phase (phase2 or phase3),
timepoint, method (assay or "not stated"), placebo_adjusted (true/false), dose (if stated).
For biomarker_change give "value" as the change (negative = reduction) and state in attrs.kind whether it is
"percent" or "absolute".

Return JSON only:
{"facts": [{"key": "...", "value": <number or string>, "unit": "...", "attrs": {...}, "quote": "..."}]}
prompt:
Trial: SPIRE-2 NCT01975389 - The Evaluation of Bococizumab (PF-04950615; RN316) in Reducing the Occurrence of Major Cardiovascular Events in High Risk Subjects
Investigational drug: bococizumab
Document: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT01975389 SPIRE-2 (registry, published 2013-11-04, source ctgov:NCT01975389@2017-03-17)

--- DOCUMENT TEXT ---
ClinicalTrials.gov record NCT01975389 (SPIRE-2)
Title: The Evaluation of Bococizumab (PF-04950615; RN316) in Reducing the Occurrence of Major Cardiovascular Events in High Risk Subjects
Official title: Phase 3 Multi Center, Double Blind, Randomized, Placebo Controlled, Parallel Group Evaluation Of The Efficacy, Safety, And Tolerability Of Bococizumab (Pf-04950615), In Reducing The Occurrence Of Major Cardiovascular Events In High Risk Subjects
Sponsor: Pfizer
Phase: PHASE3
Conditions: Cardiovascular Disease
Interventions: bococizumab (PF-04950615) (DRUG); Placebo (DRUG)
Start date: 2013-10-29
Enrollment: 10564 (ACTUAL)
Primary outcome(s): Event Rate Per 100 Participant-years for First Occurrence of Major Cardiovascular (CV) Event [From baseline until the date of first adjudicated and confirmed occurrence of major CV event (maximum duration: up to 3.4 years)]
Eligibility criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Must be on background lipid lowering treatment.
* Must be at high risk of a CV event.
* Must have an LDL C \>/=100 mg/dL (2.6 mmol/L) OR non HDL C \>/=130 mg/dL (3.4 mmol/L).

Exclusion Criteria:

* Planned coronary (PCI or CABG) or other arterial revascularization.
* New York Heart Association Class IV congestive heart failure or left ventricular ejection fraction \< 25% by cardiac imaging.
* Chronic renal insufficiency with creatinine clearance of \<30 ml/min/1.73m\^2 by MDRD formula or with end state renal disease on dialysis.
* History of hemorrhagic stroke.
* Prior exposure to bococizumab or other investigational PCSK9 inhibitor.
Brief summary: This study evaluates the PCSK9 inhibitor, Bococizumab (PF-04950615;RN316), compared to placebo, in reducing the occurrrence of major cardiovascular events, including cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction, stroke, and unstable angina requiring urgent revascularization in high risk subjects who are receiving background lipid lowering therapy and have cholesterol laboratory values of LDL-C \>/= 100 mg/dL (2.6 mmol/L) or non-HDL-C \>/=130 mg/dL (3.4 mmol/L).
--- END ---
